findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: There was observed to be raw fish submerged in water to thaw. The water was not running, allowing the water in the bucket to reach above 41F. CORRECTED- Water was ran over the bucket of fish to allow it to thaw correctly and the employee was educated on proper thawing. Ensure that TCS food is thawed through refrigeration, under cold running water, or through the cooking process. 

 TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17: Observed large pan of cooked chicken wings with no use by date. Pan of wings was labeled with proper use by date during inspection. (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

(C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

(C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17: Observed several bucket with several pre-portioned bags of pot roast to be datemarked 3/3. All bags of pot roast were discarded. (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: 3-305.11: Observed portion cup used as a scoop in container of sugar in spice dry storage area. Use a scoop with a handle to avoid contamination. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.comment: 4-602.11: (A) Observed ice machine baffles in dish room and kitchen to be soiled with debris. findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.130 & 140 - A) Seasoning shakers and squeeze bottles of liquids in cooking and prep areas were not labeled. Unless the identity of a product is unmistakable foods, such as salt, flour, water, and seasonings, not in the original packaging shall be stored in containers identifying the products by their common name. Provide labels for squeeze bottles and seasoning shakers.   
B) Pot roast made today was portioned and cooling in the walkin cooler. The time was not marked on the label (see #3d). Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Shredded cheese and cheese slices in top holding areas of pizza cooler and large prep cooler had internal temperatures of 50F. Containers holding products were sitting on top edges of other containers and were not down in contact with cold air. Both products were discarded in the trash. Employees were advised on cold holding and proper storage in upper holding areas of prep coolers. Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - A) Pot roast portioned in plastic baggies and stored in a large plastic container in the walkin cooler had internal temperatures of 84F-96F. Date on label was 10/24, but no time was indicated. Owner verified the pot roast was pulled from oven at ~1:30-2p. Temperature was checked around 2:30p. Owner was allowed to keep pot roast, and portions were placed on a backing sheet in the walkin freezer to help rapidly drop the temperature.  B) Four pans of cheese sauce with prep date 10/24 stacked together in walkin cooler had surface temperatures at 40F-45F. Internal temperatures for cheese sauce in the middle two containers were at 49F and 54F. Cheese sauce in bottom container had internal temperature of 47, and cheese sauce in top container had internal temperature of 41F-42F. Cheese sauce above 42F was discarded in the trash by owner. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below within additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours. Allow heat to vent off of cooling foods and do not store hot products stacked together in pans or in baggies when foods are still hot. Utilize ice baths, the walkin freezer, and ice wands to help rapidly cool cooked foods.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text: 750.830 - A lid in clean equipment storage had cheese sauce stuck on it. A small bowl stored by mashed potato hot holding had food debris still stuck on the bottom. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine. If food debris and/or other soil remains after process has been completed then repeat the aforementioned steps as many times as necessary to remove soil and properly clean/sanitize all surfaces.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Sanitizer solution by grill had concentration below 100ppm chlorine. Solution was soiled. Solution was remade during the inspection. Maintain sanitizer solutions at 100ppm chlorine. Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) pizza slicer; B) top inside microwave across from pizza cooler (dried food splash); C) soda gun where nozzle attaches (mold); & D) can opener blade (dried food debris). Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **Apply 4hr rule to in-use utensils such as slicers, knives, whisks, etc. Up to every 4hrs switch out said utensils, cutting boards, etc. with clean utensils and equipment. Clean and sanitize the can opener up to every 4hrs as well.**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) fryers (inside panels around mechanicals, undersides, and wheels); B) drain line and condensate line underneath large ice machine in side room (mold/buildup); & C) area between two lids on top holding area of pizza cooler (crumbs). Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - (R) Pans of cheese sauce (6 total) and chili (2 total) prepared on 5/28 had prep times of 7pm and 8:30pm. Surface temperatures ranged from 53F-81F, and internal temperatures ranged from 64F-90F. Pans were stacked together, and condensation was observed inside the lids. Cheese sauce and chili (~30 to 40 gallons total) were discarded. Cooked potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in additional 4hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to monitor temperatures to ensure foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in designated time frame during cooling process in the freezer and on ice baths. **Educational handout on quick chill of cooked PHF was provided**

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 & 280 - Employee was observed handling lemons with bare hands. Lemons were being sliced and zested for sauce being made that would not be cooked. Lemons and zest were discarded. Employee washed his hands and put on a pair of gloves prior to starting prep again. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Use suitable utensils (i.e. tongs, scoops, etc.) or wear gloves when handling ready to eat foods

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750.160b - Employee doing food prep was observed walking out the back door by the dish area wearing a pair of single use gloves. Employee came back in from outside and went right back to food prep area without removing gloves. Employee removed gloves, washed his hands, and put on a new pair of gloves at request of inspector. Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task. Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations. **Educational handouts on handwashing and proper glove use were provided including IL Food Code Section 750.510 on proper handwashing technique**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Shelf in reach-in section of 3 door bar cooler had peeling paint and rust was starting to form (section where Copper Ridge wine was located). Repaint or replace the shelf. B) Wooden shelves in wine cooler at bar had spots that felt rough, and the upper shelf had white mold growth on the back edge. Clean and re-surface the shelves or replace them. C) Small microwave in back prep had bottom plate missing and side was pulling off. Dust/debris buildup were observed along the side and underneath the microwave. Clean the side and underneath the microwave and provide proper repairs to eliminate buildup of debris. Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth, easily cleanable, and in good repair.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) BAR - 1) (R) inside ice machine (mold), 2) (R) east end soda gun nozzle (mold around seal) & 3) ice scoop holder (east end of bar); B) scoop holder at spice storage shelves; & C) magnetic knife strip at pizza cooler. Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **Make sure nozzles and diffusers to soda machine are getting scrubbed and not just soaked. The only way to remove gross buildup is to physically scrub them**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) SIDE ROOM - 1) roll carts, 2) lower ledges/metal covers on cooler & freezer, 3) bottom inside cooler, & 4) cabinet above 3 part sink; B) BAR - 1) reach-in section of 3 door cooler (south end - splash), 2) shelf inside wine cooler (mold), 3) edges of beer cooler door seals, & 4) under hard plastic liners on back of beer coolers; C) spice storage shelves (pan holding instant tapioca, etc.); D) (R) dessert cooler shelves; E) DRY STORAGE - 1) (R) bulk cracker bin storage shelf, 2) (R) gray bins holding dry goods, & 3) inside bulk cracker tubs. Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
